video.title: This app is making $2,000 PER DAY

summary: Starter Story interviews a former Google engineer and serial founder (transcribed as Rastie Turek) who built an encrypted on-device file and photo vault iPhone app (transcribed 'Voltaire') in about three weeks entirely with coding agents. It made 66 USD in month one and 41,000 USD in month six, now ~2,000-3,000 USD a day, with lifetime purchases (39.99 USD) making most revenue. Growth came from SEO, not ads: Claude runs each morning to find keywords with impressions but no clicks, writes one quality guide a day and adds internal links, and web visitors convert ~10% to the app. Takeaway: a simple app in a proven category plus an agent-run SEO loop can be almost fully automated.

speakers.name: Rastie Turek
speakers.description: Founder of the encrypted vault app; ex-Google, prior exits (name as transcribed by Whisper)

ideas.name: Encrypted on-device file and photo vault iOS app
ideas.one_liner: A simple Dropbox-like iPhone app that encrypts files and photos on device with no servers or shared keys, monetised by freemium upgrades, mostly lifetime purchases.
ideas.business_model: Freemium iOS app: weekly, annual and lifetime in-app purchases; lifetime is ~60% of purchases and 80%+ of revenue.
ideas.customer: Privacy-conscious iPhone users storing IDs, birth certificates, crypto wallet keys and sensitive photos
ideas.problem: Need to keep sensitive files close to the device but private; incumbent vault apps are old and neglected
ideas.offer: Pattern-unlocked encrypted vaults (~52 billion possible) with no recovery and no way to tell what is stored

pricing.model: Freemium with subscriptions and lifetime purchase
pricing.notes: Whisper transcript gives weekly '1 99' and annual '1999'; read as 1.99/week and 19.99/year. Conversion is lowest on day 1 (5.47%) and rises by day 35-60.

acquisition_channels.details: Agent-written marketing site and how-to guides targeting every keyword that points to the App Store category on the web; one high-quality guide a day; web is the majority of traffic and converts ~10% to the app.

quote.text: what if I try to pull in every keyword that is out there, that essentially points to the same thing as an app store, but on the web
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

acquisition_channels.details: Apple Search (App Store search) is a major download source.

ideas.delivery: Solo founder; app built in ~3 weeks entirely with coding agents; Claude runs each morning to find impression-but-no-click keywords via Google Search Console/Keyword Planner MCP tools, writes and publishes a guide and adds internal links.
unit_economics_claims: 41,000 USD in a single month six months later
tools: gum (his open-source CLI/MCP over Google services)
ideas.startup_cost: Minimal (coding agents, Apple developer account; not stated)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First month (66 USD); scaled over ~6 months

acquisition.how: Agent-run daily SEO loop: keyword discovery, guide writing, publishing and internal linking; App Store search is inbound. Fully legal in the UK.

onboarding.how: Self-serve App Store download and onboarding.

support.how: Few support needs; a paid tier was added partly to reduce feature requests.

uk_applicability.notes: Works the same in the UK: App Store is global; no servers means minimal UK GDPR data-processing exposure. Note law-enforcement requests (he was contacted by the FBI) and UK Investigatory Powers Act notices could be a consideration for encryption apps.

risks: Crowded category with large old competitors
Dependence on Google rankings and App Store policies
No data recovery may cause unhappy users
Low MRR since most buy lifetime

tactics.name: Daily agent SEO loop
steps: Each morning an agent queries Google Search Console/Keyword Planner via MCP tools
Find keywords with impressions but no clicks (e.g. 16,000 impressions at position ~50)
Write one high-quality guide targeting that keyword
Publish and add internal links from existing high-traffic pages
Wait 3-4 days for indexing and watch traffic and conversions

quote.text: it runs through keyboard planner every single morning, looks at all the traffic, it identifies keywords that are being surfaced, but not essentially being driven to the site
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

tactics.name: Place CTAs where readers stop
steps: Have agents analyse where readers commonly end in an article
Put App Store CTAs at those points

quote.text: wherever people are like, commonly ending, I want them to be able to go through the app
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

tactics.name: Attack neglected incumbents' web keywords
steps: Pick a proven App Store category whose incumbents are 15+ years old
Accept you cannot outrank them in the App Store
Capture the same intent on the open web with guides

quote.text: Most of the apps in this area are 15 years or older. They have millions of users
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

tactics.name: Monetise to filter feature requests
steps: Launch free with a few paid advanced features
Offer weekly, annual and lifetime tiers
Expect conversion to rise over 30-60 days for utility apps

quote.text: if users are sending me separate requests, I just don't want to be bothered as much
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

lessons.lesson: Proven, simple app categories with neglected incumbents are winnable; no new idea needed.

quote.text: An app like this and a founder like Rasti is proof that you do not need a brand new or complicated idea to win
quote.speaker: Pat Walls

lessons.lesson: SEO still works for niche intent when content is high quality and internally linked.
Utility apps can convert late (day 35-60) unlike hype apps that must convert on day one.

quote.text: I have the lowest conversion day one and I have the highest conversion like day 60
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

lessons.lesson: Coding agents let a domain outsider ship a paid iOS app in weeks.
A one-person app with free tooling can run with near-zero costs and nothing to break.

quote.text: you can really run things for free. You know, there's like nothing to break
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek

lessons.lesson: Lifetime pricing can dominate revenue for privacy/utility apps.
Get better slightly every day rather than overthinking how things should be done.

quote.text: every day just be slightly better than they they before
quote.speaker: Rastie Turek
